DDPM on MNIST — results

A 2.21M-parameter convolutional U-Net, 10,000 training steps, 11.4 minutes: FID 45.57 ± 0.26 at n=1000 against a 12.19 real-vs-real floor measured with the same code and the same sample count.

1What was trained

ModelSimpleUNet (unet_simple.py) — conv3×3 + BatchNorm + ReLU, MaxPool down, Upsample+skip-concat up, timestep as a per-channel bias (drawn below)
Parameters2,212,481
Not usedattention, residual blocks, transformer, zero-init — none of it
DiffusionT = 1000, linear β from 1e-4 to 0.02, ε-prediction, plain MSE
OptimizerAdam, lr 3e-4, batch 256, 10,000 steps
DataMNIST 28×28 nearest-upscaled to 32×32, scaled to [0,1]
Time11.4 min (68 ms/step at the end), single GPU

Loss fell 0.0688 → 0.0151 (4.5×). FID fell 86.3 → 45.3 (2×), which is the point of the graph below: training loss is not a quality metric.

2How one image is made

x = torch.randn(1, 1, 32, 32)              # start from pure noise  (t = 1000)
for t in range(1000, 0, -1):               # 1000 reverse steps
    eps = model(x, t)                      # predict the noise in x
    x = 1/sqrt(α_t) * (x - (1-α_t)/sqrt(1-ᾱ_t) * eps) + sqrt(β_t) * z
return x.clamp(0, 1)                       # a 32×32 digit

The schedule is below: signal √ᾱ dies from 1 to 0.006 as noise √(1−ᾱ) rises to 1.

The classifier is a small CNN trained on the same 32×32 grid: 97.85% on 2,000 held-out images.

Read this table as: FID 45.6 is not “close to real”, it is better than noise by 9× and worse than real data by 3.7×. Same for KID. Precision/recall must be compared to their own floor — 0.573/0.640 is what real data scores against itself at n=1000 in 2048 dimensions, not 1.0.

5The number that makes FID honest

FID is biased at small n. Measuring real-vs-real with the same n exposes the bias:

nmodelfloornoise
10086.6753.64430.9
25061.8432.56422.5
50054.9520.36415.5
100045.3112.19413.2

At n=100 the floor alone (53.64) is higher than the model’s score at n=1000 (45.31). Any FID quoted without its n and a matched floor is uninterpretable.

6Why I trust the FID (five checks)

  1. Same preprocessing as pytorch-fid: PIL→RGB→ToTensor→bilinear 299→ 2x−1→block3→mean over H,W. Inception weights are the library’s own cached checkpoint.
  2. Same square root as the library: 20/20 FID computations used scipy.linalg.sqrtm on S1·S2, exactly the call calculate_frechet_distance makes. Zero fallbacks (fid_sqrt_method: {sqrtm: 20, eigh: 0}).
  3. Cross-check against the library’s CLI, on the same device: ours 45.3064 vs python -m pytorch_fid 45.3064, difference 4.7e-06.
  4. Device matters, and that is measured too: the same CLI on CPU gives 45.2507, i.e. a 0.056 gap from cuDNN vs CPU float32 convolution. Comparing a GPU feature set to a CPU run measures kernel noise, not methodology — so the check runs both.
  5. A real bug was found this way and fixed: PNG export originally used .astype(np.uint8), which truncates instead of rounding, darkening every pixel by up to 1/255. That alone moved FID by ~1.8, more than 2,500 training steps were worth. The cross-check is what caught it; the code now rounds.

7Failure modes I tested

No catastrophic failure (no memorized copies, no collapsed classes), but two real weaknesses show up.

checkresultgraph
Memorization — L2 to nearest training image generated median 4.78 vs real 5.01; min 1.47, no mass near 0 → no copies g09
Mode collapse — predicted class histogram all 10 digits present, but 1s over-generated: 26.6% vs 12.7% → imbalance, not collapse g07
Coverage — precision/recall 0.113 / 0.135: low precision and low recall vs floor, i.e. blurry and not fully covering g06
Classifier confidence 0.927 vs real 0.969 → recognizable digits, slightly less crisp g08
Forward process unit test — fixed x₀, 500 noise draws mean and std of x_t match √ᾱ·x₀ and √(1−ᾱ) to ≤0.036 per pixel, within Monte-Carlo noise (0.045) —
Denoising loss vs t 0.368 at t=1 → 0.0008 at t=1000 g10

The per-timestep curve is high at low t on purpose: at t=1 almost every pixel of an MNIST image is background (x₀≈0), so x_t ≈ 0.01·ε and the noise is recoverable; at t=1000 x_t ≈ ε, so predicting zero error is trivial. It is not a sign of undertraining.

10What I do not claim

  • Not “U-Net with attention”, not a transformer, not latent diffusion, not DDIM. Plain ε-prediction DDPM.
  • 45.6 is not comparable to published MNIST FIDs: different splits, n, resampling and preprocessing. It is only comparable to the 12.19 floor measured here, under this protocol.
  • Only one architecture was trained. unet.py (35.7M), TinyUNet, DiT, ConvNet, MLP have parameter counts and timings in denoisers.py, no trained metrics.
  • 3 sampling seeds only at the final checkpoint; 25/50/75% use seed 0.
  • No Inception Score, no FID-vs-published-baseline table, no resume-from-checkpoint (the original run did not save optimizer state; the field is null rather than fake).

11Interview version, in four sentences

I trained a 2.2M-parameter conv U-Net as the DDPM noise predictor on MNIST, 10k steps in 11 minutes. FID is 45.6 ± 0.3 at n=1000 against a 12.2 real-vs-real floor measured with the same code and sample count, and it improves monotonically from 86.3 at 2.5k steps.

I verified the metric against pytorch-fid’s own CLI to 5e-06, which caught a real uint8-truncation bug in my PNG export, and I report the floor because FID at n=100 is 53.6 even for real data.

The model covers all ten digits with no memorized copies, but it over-produces 1s and its precision/recall are both below the floor — so it is a correct, modest model, not a state-of-the-art one.
